questions.prompt: Which protocol transfers files between a client and server?
questions.fact: It sends credentials in plain text, which is why secure variants replaced it for anything sensitive.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a semiconductor fabrication plant?
questions.fact: A modern one costs upward of twenty billion dollars and must be cleaner than an operating theatre.

questions.prompt: Which company owns LinkedIn?
questions.fact: It was acquired in 2016 for around twenty-six billion dollars, one of the largest software deals at the time.

questions.prompt: What does the acronym UX designer primarily study?
questions.fact: Much of the work is watching people fail to do something, which is more informative than asking them.

questions.prompt: Which technology uses radio waves to identify tagged objects?
questions.fact: Passive tags need no battery, drawing all the power they use from the reader's own signal.

questions.prompt: What is the term for a company's move to newer systems from legacy ones?
questions.fact: Some banking systems still run code written in the 1960s, because migrating it is riskier than maintaining it.

questions.prompt: Which company produces the Unreal game engine?
questions.fact: It is now used widely outside gaming, including for film backgrounds and architectural visualisation.

questions.prompt: What does the acronym OCR do?
options: Converts images of text into text
questions.fact: Early systems were trained on a single typeface, which is why documents had to be printed in a specific font.

questions.prompt: Which term describes computing performed near the data source rather than centrally?
questions.fact: Self-driving cars rely on it, because sending sensor data to a distant server and back is far too slow.

questions.prompt: Which company created the Postgres database?
questions.fact: It began at Berkeley in the 1980s and has been developed by an open community ever since.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a checksum?
questions.fact: Bank card numbers include one, which is why a single mistyped digit is usually rejected instantly.

questions.prompt: Which company developed the Kotlin programming language?
questions.fact: Google later made it the preferred language for Android, though it was not the company that created it.

questions.prompt: What does the acronym CI stand for in software delivery?
questions.fact: The point is merging small changes often, so conflicts stay small enough to resolve in minutes.

questions.prompt: Which company makes the Photoshop alternative Affinity Photo?
questions.fact: It sold as a one-off purchase during a period when nearly all competitors moved to subscriptions.

questions.prompt: What is the term for software running below the operating system on hardware?
questions.fact: It is stored on the device itself, which is why a bad update can leave hardware permanently unusable.

questions.prompt: Which company created the Signal messaging app?
questions.fact: Its encryption protocol is used by several competitors, including WhatsApp, under an open licence.

questions.prompt: What does the acronym HDR improve in photography?
questions.fact: It works by combining several exposures, which is why moving subjects can produce ghosting.

questions.prompt: Which term describes a piece of code that runs on a schedule?
questions.fact: Its syntax of five fields is famously unmemorable, and most people look it up every single time.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a reverse proxy?
options: Sitting in front of servers to handle requests
questions.fact: It commonly handles encryption too, so the servers behind it can exchange plain traffic internally.

questions.prompt: What does the acronym SLA define?
questions.fact: Uptime figures are often quoted in nines, where five nines allows about five minutes of downtime a year.

questions.prompt: Which company produced the first commercially successful digital camera for consumers?
questions.fact: It invented the digital camera in 1975 and shelved it, fearing damage to its film business.

questions.prompt: What is the term for splitting a database across multiple machines?
questions.fact: It makes queries that span shards far more expensive, which is why the split point matters enormously.

questions.prompt: Which company created the Ruby on Rails framework?
questions.fact: It was extracted from an existing product rather than designed in advance, which shaped its opinionated defaults.

questions.prompt: What does the acronym P2P describe?
questions.fact: BitTorrent works by having downloaders simultaneously upload, so popular files transfer faster rather than slower.

questions.prompt: Which company created the Vim text editor's predecessor, vi?
questions.fact: Its keyboard shortcuts assume a terminal without arrow keys, which is why movement uses letters.

questions.prompt: What is the term for the practice of hiding a system's internal detail?
questions.fact: Every layer of a computer is one, which is why you can use a phone without knowing what a transistor is.

questions.prompt: Which company makes the Chromebook operating system?
questions.fact: It runs a Linux kernel underneath, and can now run Android and Linux applications alongside web ones.

questions.prompt: What does the acronym TCP guarantee that UDP does not?
questions.fact: Video calls often prefer UDP, because a lost frame arriving late is worse than never arriving at all.

questions.prompt: Which company developed the Erlang programming language?
questions.fact: It was built for telephone exchanges, where systems must keep running while being upgraded.

questions.prompt: What is the term for code left in place that no longer runs?
questions.fact: Compilers usually strip it out, but it still costs human time every time someone reads the file.

questions.prompt: Which company created the Docker container platform?
questions.fact: The underlying kernel features already existed for years; its contribution was making them usable.

questions.prompt: What does the acronym GDPR regulate?
questions.fact: It applies to any organisation handling EU residents' data, regardless of where that organisation is based.

questions.prompt: Which company created the Elasticsearch search engine?
questions.fact: Its licence change in 2021 prompted Amazon to fork it, creating a competing open version.

questions.prompt: What is the term for a temporary failure that resolves itself on retry?
questions.fact: Retrying too eagerly can turn a small outage into a large one, which is why backoff delays exist.

questions.prompt: Which company created the Figma design tool?
questions.fact: Running entirely in the browser let several designers edit the same file simultaneously, which was its main advantage.

questions.prompt: What does the acronym WYSIWYG describe?
questions.fact: Before it, formatting was written as visible codes and you found out how it looked only after printing.

questions.prompt: Which company produced the first web browser with tabbed browsing in wide use?
questions.fact: It also pioneered mouse gestures and built-in ad blocking years before rivals adopted either.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a linter?
questions.fact: The name comes from a Unix tool that picked out bits of fluff from C programs, like lint from clothing.

questions.prompt: Which company created the Node.js runtime?
questions.fact: It put JavaScript on the server by embedding the engine Google had built for Chrome.

questions.prompt: What does the acronym EV charging term kWh measure?
questions.fact: Power is measured in kilowatts; multiplying by time gives energy, which is what a battery actually stores.

questions.prompt: Which company created the Steam games platform?
questions.fact: It was launched to deliver patches for the company's own games and was widely resented by players at first.

questions.prompt: What is the term for testing how a system behaves under heavy demand?
questions.fact: Systems often fail in unexpected places under load, such as logging, rather than in the code being tested.

questions.prompt: Which company created the TypeScript language?
questions.fact: It compiles to plain JavaScript, so it adds checking at development time and disappears entirely at runtime.

questions.prompt: What does the acronym API gateway do?
questions.fact: It usually handles authentication and rate limiting too, so individual services do not each reimplement them.

questions.prompt: Which company developed the LLVM compiler infrastructure?
questions.fact: It began as a research project in Illinois and now underpins compilers for a long list of languages.

questions.prompt: What is the term for a system that continues working despite component failure?
questions.fact: Aircraft control systems often run three computers and take the majority answer when they disagree.

questions.prompt: Which company created the Blender 3D software?
questions.fact: It was bought out of a failing company by a community fundraiser and released as open source in 2002.

questions.prompt: What does the acronym MVP stand for in product development?
questions.fact: The point is learning what people actually want, which is why shipping a polished wrong thing is the failure mode.

questions.prompt: Which company created the Terraform infrastructure tool?
questions.fact: Describing infrastructure as code means a whole environment can be recreated from a file rather than from memory.

questions.prompt: What is the term for storing computed results to avoid recalculating?
questions.fact: It turns some naively slow algorithms into fast ones without changing the logic at all.

questions.prompt: Which company created the Slack competitor Microsoft Teams?
questions.fact: Bundling it with existing office subscriptions triggered a European competition complaint.

questions.prompt: What does the acronym LiDAR measure using?
questions.fact: Archaeologists use it to find structures under forest canopy, which has rewritten the map of the Maya world.
